svg.aria-label: A world map centred on the Indian and Pacific oceans showing where oil is flowing in September 2026. A gold ribbon from the Persian Gulf to China, Japan, Korea and India is drawn thin and dashed, labelled cut roughly in half. An orange ribbon from the US Gulf Coast to Asia is labelled 3.3 million barrels a day, three times pre-war. A blue ribbon from Venezuela to the United States is labelled 0.79 million barrels a day, a seven-year high. Magenta ribbons from Russia to India and China are labelled record volumes.
svg.text: Where the oil is going now
the flows the closure created, September 2026 — width proportional to million barrels a day
Gulf → Asia: cut roughly in half
(84% of Hormuz crude went to Asia)
Dashed = a pre-war flow that has been cut back; solid = a flow the closure created or enlarged. US crude to Asia 3.29 mb/d (EIA/Reuters, May);
Venezuela → US 786 kb/d (July, a seven-year high); Russia → India record two months running (CREA, July); Yanbu 5 mb/d until 10 Sep.
Routes are schematic — origin, destination and size, not the track a tanker sails. Centred on the Indian and Pacific oceans, so the Atlantic is off the edge. Natural Earth.
